title: XII: The Minister’s Vigil

teacherSummary.text: One May midnight, Dimmesdale climbs the scaffold and shrieks; nobody wakes except Governor Bellingham and Mistress Hibbins, who see nothing. Hester and Pearl, returning from Governor Winthrop's deathbed, join him hand in hand. Pearl asks if he will stand with them at noon; he says no. A meteor lights the sky in the shape of an A, and Chillingworth is seen watching. Next day the sexton returns the minister's glove and reports the A in the sky means Angel.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Wilt thou stand here with mother and me, tomorrow noontide” slowly and put it in my own words: On the midnight scaffold, Pearl asks whether he will stand there with her mother and her at noon tomorrow. Next, craft. I notice the simple child's question, which demands in daylight what he will only do in the dark. The strongest word is “noontide”: it means full noon, when the whole town would see them together. Then, effect. What is Pearl really asking Dimmesdale to do? My answer: Pearl asks for public acknowledgment; when Dimmesdale refuses and says "not tomorrow," the scene shows his fear and sets up his final confession on the same scaffold in daylight.
